body:
This is a purely claude-driven PR, so I am not sure it is even right because I do not know the methods that it uses in the detail, but it is supposed to answer to https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/discussions/6248. In practice at every construction of a `Distributed` architecture we check that the configuration is correct and we spit out a warning otherwise. The checks are that (1) the threads are correctly assigned (2) the ranks see the closest GPU possible (3) the device memory is correctly configured.

Claude explains it better
> ## Warn about misconfigured MPI / GPU setups in `Distributed`
> 
> Motivated by #6248: several cluster settings slow multi-GPU runs by 3–9× (or crash NCCL) without any error. `Distributed()` and `NCCLDistributed()` now check the configuration once at construction and warn on rank 0, with the number of affected ranks, when:
> 
> - MPI was initialized without `MPI_THREAD_MULTIPLE` although spare Julia threads exist (the halo progress worker is disabled)
> - a rank has fewer CPU cores than Julia threads (Linux)
> - MPI is not CUDA-aware (`MPIX_Query_cuda_support` from the loaded `libmpi`, which also works behind MPItrampoline; `MPICH_GPU_SUPPORT_ENABLED` on Cray)
> - several ranks share one GPU
> - each rank sees only its own GPU (e.g. Slurm's `--gpus-per-task`)
> - CUDA.jl's memory pool prevents CUDA IPC between ranks on the same node
> - a rank runs on CPU cores that are not attached to its GPU
> 
> The CUDA-aware and memory-pool checks are skipped for `NCCLDistributed`, which does not pass GPU buffers to MPI.
> 
> Implementation: `Distributed()` builds the architecture with `distributed_architecture` (the former constructor body) and > then calls `validate_distributed_configuration(arch)`. `NCCLDistributed` and `TransposableField` use the builder, so each > warning prints once. The GPU facts come from `gpu_configuration` in the CUDA extension.
> 
> Tests: `test/distributed/configuration.jl` runs misconfigured and correct setups under `mpiexec`; it is added to the  Distributed MPI CI job. Verified on 2 GPUs on two sockets: each warning fires in its misconfiguration, a correct setup prints none, and `NCCLDistributed` prints none.
> 
> Note: the Buildkite GPU distributed jobs use `slurm_gpus_per_task: 1` and keep the memory pool on, so they will now print those two warnings.

cc @francispoulin maybe you want to test this on your cluster to see if the offending configurations trigger a warning?

body:
I believe the code change makes sense (`do` blocks can be problematic in some cases when they capture local variables), but the added test feels a bit overspecific, but I can't think of anything else, happy to remove it.  https://github.com/NumericalEarth/Breeze.jl/pull/1207 is a targeted fix to Breeze to avoid the same issue, but making it more general here in Oceananigans is good as well.

> `initialize_jld2_file!` specialized on the outputs, and captured each one in a `jldopen` do-block closure. When an output is a large immutable struct, for example a field of a `KernelFunctionOperation` whose kernel function captures many fields, at `-O0` the function and that closure reserved megabytes of stack. Together they overflowed the 4 MiB stack of a task. Breeze's P3 process-rate diagnostics hit this in CI on Julia 1.11 with `--optimize=0`, where ParallelTestRunner runs test files inside tasks.
> 
> Mark `outputs` and `model` `@nospecialize`, as
> `save_and_serialize_properties!` already does, since initialization runs once. Also open the file without a do block in the per-output loop, so no closure specializes on an output.
> 
> With a 25 KB output field, the writer path now runs within a 0.5 MiB task stack at `-O0`. Before this change it overflowed the default 4 MiB stack: about 3.4 MB came from `initialize_jld2_file!` and about 1 MB from the closure.
title: Do not specialize JLD2Writer file initialization on the outputs

body:
## Summary

Splits the Stokes-drift abstraction into two concrete subtypes of a new `AbstractStokesDrift` supertype:

- **`StokesDrift`** (function mode, fully backward-compatible): all derivative slots are callables `f(x, y, z, t[, params])`. Restored to its original 10-parameter form; no `uˢ, vˢ, wˢ` slots, no Field dispatch, no validation. Existing user code is unchanged.
- **`FieldStokesDrift`** (Field mode): six prognostic `Field` slots (`uˢ, vˢ, wˢ, ∂t_uˢ, ∂t_vˢ, ∂t_wˢ`) at the C-grid velocity locations for couplings where the Stokes drift comes from an external wave model.

```julia
sd = FieldStokesDrift(grid)                          # all six Fields default-allocated
sd = FieldStokesDrift(grid; uˢ=my_uˢ_field)          # override individual slots
NonhydrostaticModel(grid; stokes_drift=sd, ...)
```

The 7-parameter `FieldStokesDrift` struct stores only the Field slots — no dead `zerofunction` placeholders. The per-slot kwarg constructor defaults each missing argument to a freshly-allocated `Field` at the matching staggered location, so callers can share Fields with other code by overriding individual kwargs.

## Behavior

- Spatial derivatives in `x_curl_Uˢ_cross_U, y_curl_Uˢ_cross_U, z_curl_Uˢ_cross_U` are computed inline from the stored `uˢ, vˢ, wˢ` Fields via the staggered FD operators (`∂xᶠᶠᶜ, ∂yᶠᶠᶜ, ∂zᶠᶜᶠ, ∂zᶜᶠᶠ, ∂xᶠᶜᶠ, ∂yᶜᶠᶠ` + `ℑ` interpolators). Both `∂z uˢ, ∂z vˢ` and the cross-derivative terms `∂y uˢ, ∂x vˢ` participate — no curl approximation drops them.
- `∂t_uˢ, ∂t_vˢ, ∂t_wˢ` are read directly via `getindex` at the velocity location.
- `compute_stokes_drift!(::FieldStokesDrift, grid)` fills `wˢ` and `∂t_wˢ` by vertical integration of `∂_z wˢ = -∂_x uˢ - ∂_y vˢ` (same continuity pattern as the hydrostatic model's `compute_w_from_continuity!`), starting from zero at the bottom. No-op on `StokesDrift` and `UniformStokesDrift`.
- `NonhydrostaticModel.update_state!` invokes `compute_stokes_drift!` between the velocity halo fill and auxiliary-field computation, so `wˢ` and `∂t_wˢ` are always in sync with `uˢ, vˢ, ∂t_uˢ, ∂t_vˢ`.

## Shared structure

The three `*_curl_Uˢ_cross_U` methods share a single body (the `(∇×uˢ) × uᴱ` algebra) and dispatch on `Union{StokesDrift, FieldStokesDrift}`; per-derivative `_∂{x,y,z}_{u,v,w}ˢ_*` helpers branch on the concrete type. `UniformStokesDrift` retains its own specialized curl-cross methods because it has a simpler structure.

## Backward compatibility

Function-mode user code is completely unchanged. `StokesDrift(; ∂z_uˢ, ...)` returns the same struct as before, with the same type-parameter layout.

## Motivation

Developed against the wind-drift instability example in [NumericalEarth/Ripple.jl](https://github.com/NumericalEarth/Ripple.jl), where the wave-model pseudomomentum `p(z) = Q(z)·A·K` equals the deep-water Stokes drift when the wave action is calibrated to the target steepness, and the analytic pseudomomentum tendency `Q(z)·∂t(A·K)` equals the Stokes acceleration the ocean must see for the wave-mean energy budget to close.

## Test plan

`test/test_stokes_drift.jl` gains a `FieldStokesDrift` testset:

- [x] All six Field slots allocated by `FieldStokesDrift(grid)` at the expected staggered locations.
- [x] Per-slot kwarg override (e.g., `FieldStokesDrift(grid; uˢ=my_uˢ)`).
- [x] Zero state gives zero contributions.
- [x] Linear vertical shear `uˢ = α·z`, uniform `w = W` → `x_curl_Uˢ_cross_U = W·α` at every interior point.
- [x] Cross-derivative term `uˢ = β·y, v = V` → `V·β` (the term `UniformStokesDrift` drops).
- [x] `∂t_uˢ, ∂t_vˢ` read directly with the right sign.
- [x] `compute_stokes_drift!` fills `wˢ` from continuity when `uˢ, vˢ` have nonzero divergence.
- [x] `compute_stokes_drift!` is a no-op on function-mode `StokesDrift`.

All 326 Stokes-drift tests pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Split StokesDrift: function-mode StokesDrift + Field-mode FieldStokesDrift

body:
With `NCCLDistributed`, every rank finishes the simulation and then segfaults at exit
(`signal 11 ... in expression starting at none:0`, no backtrace, exit code 139/143).
The persistent NCCL communicators are only freed by their finalizers, which run after
MPI and CUDA have already shut down.

This PR registers an `atexit` hook when the first communicator is created. On a clean
exit the hook synchronizes CUDA and destroys each communicator after a barrier on its MPI
communicator. Julia runs `atexit` hooks last-in first-out, and MPI is initialized before
any NCCL communicator exists, so the hook runs before MPI's own finalizer.
`NCCL.destroy` is idempotent, so the finalizer that runs later is a no-op.

Tested with a small 8-GPU (2 nodes × 4) `HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModel` run, 10 iterations:

| | OpenMPI 5 | Cray MPICH |
|---|---|---|
| main | 4 of 8 ranks segfault at exit | clean |
| this PR | clean | clean |

I haven't added a CI test, since the crash only shows up on multi-node GPU runs with OpenMPI.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: NCCLDistributed: destroy communicators at exit so ranks don't segfault on shutdown
